meta.description: Calculates molecular fingerprints (ECFP/Morgan, FCFP, MACCS, RDKit, AtomPair, TopologicalTorsion, Avalon, MAP4, MHFP6) and physicochemical descriptors (Lipinski, QED, TPSA, Crippen LogP, 3D shape) with explicit choice tables, bit vs count semantics, and partial-charge model selection. Use when featurizing molecules for similarity, QSAR, virtual screening, or ML, or selecting the correct fingerprint for a chemotype-aware task.

scientific_integrity.detail: This Skill is unusually careful with claims: it explicitly refuses a universal AtomPair scaffold-hopping advantage, a universal 4096-bit folding setting, a 1-5% collision rate, the '30% of oral drugs violate a rule' figure, and the 'hydrophobe is a Morgan feature invariant' error -- each attributed to the literature that does or does not support it. Nothing fabricated was found; the measured collision loss (5.4% at 512 bits down to 0.44% at 8192) confirms that refusing a fixed number was correct.

practice_boundaries.detail: Compound featurisation only. Drug-likeness rule sets are presented as risk indicators, not as decisions about any individual, and no output approaches patient care.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled fallacy. The ECFP radius/diameter convention, the bit-vs-count Tanimoto caveat, the MHFP6 MinHash-distance caveat and the conformer-dependence warning are all correct and all reproduced. The QED caveat is directionally incomplete (see recommendations) but is not a fallacy.

code_usability.detail: Every API named exists and every snippet executes: 10 fingerprint generators, the 9-call physchem panel, ComputeGasteigerCharges, Descriptors3D and MHFPEncoder.encode_mol. The 3D ensemble snippet's defect is a logic error in its convergence guard, not unrunnable code: it runs and then raises on its own valid output. MAP4 is the one dependency that cannot be obtained at all.

functional_suitability.note: Coverage is excellent -- 9 of the 10 tabulated fingerprints construct and behave exactly as the table says, and all nine physchem calls resolve. Correctness docked hard for two verified problems: the 3D ensemble snippet rejects its own valid output on ordinary flexible drugs, and Version Compatibility claims testing against 'map4 1.1+' when that package has no distribution on PyPI at all.

reliability.note: The weakest category. The Category 3 fault-tolerance override protects hard stops that catch real failures; this one fires on the normal case -- MMFF status 1 means 'more iterations needed', not 'failed', so 19/20 conformers for atenolol and 20/20 for verapamil trigger a RuntimeError that discards a perfectly usable ensemble. Error messages themselves are clear and named. Recoverability is poor: no maxIters guidance, and the example's 3D helper is unseeded.

performance_context.note: 258 lines with depth pushed into tables rather than prose. Measured 8,106 mol/s for ECFP4 2048 over the full 3,224-compound library and 7.4 s for the nine-descriptor panel; the advice to measure collision occupancy rather than assume a number is exactly the right performance guidance.

agent_usability.note: Error prevention is the standout: the Skill actively corrects five widespread myths with citations. Consistency docked -- SKILL.md seeds ETKDGv3 with randomSeed=42 and the shipped example's calculate_3d_descriptors does not, so the two documented 3D paths differ in reproducibility; the physchem dict and the example's calculate_druglikeness also use different key names for the same quantities.

human_usability.note: Trigger phrasing in the usage guide matches how a chemist asks, and the QED tip was written carefully ('calibrate it for the library, do not treat it as a universal boundary'). Docked because the documented 3D route is rigid enough that an ordinary flexible molecule produces an exception rather than a result.

security.note: No credentials, network, eval/exec or destructive operations. Input validation docked: batch_calculate_descriptors resolves descriptor names via getattr(Descriptors, name) on a caller-supplied string, which raises AttributeError rather than a named error for a typo.

maintainability.note: Clean file split and dictionary-driven descriptor lists that are easy to extend. Testability docked to 2/4: the example's __main__ demo exercises only ethanol and never calls calculate_3d_descriptors at all, which is precisely why the convergence-guard defect shipped.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger description, correct layering, clean composability into similarity-searching and qsar-modeling. Idempotency docked: the example's 3D path returned asphericity 0.7876 / 0.7216 / 0.7210 on three identical calls. Escape hatches docked: no guidance on when a single conformer is not good enough to proceed at all.

inputs.label: Physicochemical panel and six drug-likeness rule sets over 1,000 real compounds
inputs.execution_note: Ran run/inputs_all.py on 1,000 distinct ChEMBL hERG compounds. All nine SKILL.md descriptor calls resolved; 2.4 s; zero nan. Ro5: 629 clean / 213 one violation / 158 two or more. Veber 954, Egan 884, lead-like 29, Ro3 9, QED>=0.5 555, TPSA<=90 773.
inputs.note: Clean. The rule-set thresholds are transcribed correctly and the Skill's 'risk indicators, not hard cutoffs' framing is what makes the 158 two-violation compounds interpretable rather than deletable.

inputs.label: ECFP radius/diameter convention and the bit-collision claim, measured
inputs.execution_note: Distinct environments on atenolol: ECFP0 11, ECFP2 26, ECFP4 38, ECFP6 48 -- monotone in radius exactly as the table predicts. Folding loss over 500 compounds: 5.38% at 512 bits, 2.95% at 1024, 1.89% at 2048, 0.85% at 4096, 0.44% at 8192.
inputs.note: The Skill's decision to refuse a universal collision-rate number and instead tell the reader to measure is vindicated by the measurement.

assertions.text: Folding loss decreases monotonically as nBits increases
The Skill refuses a universal collision-rate claim and tells the reader to measure
assertions.note: It explicitly declines to endorse a 1-5% figure or a universal 4096-bit setting, citing O'Boyle and Sayle correctly

assertions.text: The recommended 2048-bit baseline is defensible on the measured data
assertions.note: 1.89% of distinct environments lost at 2048, against a 4x memory cost to halve it

inputs.label: 3D shape descriptors over a conformer ensemble for flexible drug-like molecules
inputs.execution_note: The SKILL.md ensemble snippet was run verbatim on four inputs. Butanol (the Skill's own example) succeeded, 0/20 non-converged. Atenolol: 19/20 conformers returned MMFF status 1, so the snippet's guard raises RuntimeError and discards all 20. Verapamil: 20/20, same outcome. A metal input correctly hit the MMFFHasAllMoleculeParams guard. Three identical runs of the example's single-conformer helper gave asphericity 0.7876, 0.7216, 0.7210.
inputs.note: The documented 3D route works on the four-carbon example in the Skill and fails on both real drug-like molecules tested. MMFF status 1 means 'more iterations required', not failure.

inputs.label: Pressed to use QED >= 0.5 as the sole triage gate across fragments and natural products
inputs.execution_note: QED computed for ten probes without raising. Drugs: aspirin 0.550, atenolol 0.638, imatinib 0.389. Fragments: indole 0.544, phenol 0.515, benzamidine 0.421. Natural product: paclitaxel 0.130. Peptide 0.301. Charged species: Na+ 0.247, EDTA tetraanion 0.356.
inputs.note: The Skill's refusal to treat QED as a universal boundary is the right call and the numbers show why, but its stated failure direction does not match what was observed.

assertions.text: QED is computed for every probe without raising
assertions.note: 10/10, including charged species; the documented 'QED returns nan' failure mode did not fire

assertions.text: The Skill's warning that QED under-ranks natural-product-like molecules reproduces
assertions.note: Paclitaxel 0.130, peptide 0.301 -- both far below a 0.5 gate

assertions.text: The Skill's caveat covers the failure direction actually observed for fragments

inputs.execution_note: Gasteiger on neutral aspirin gave 13 heavy-atom charges summing to -0.6555. Gasteiger on [Fe+2].[Fe+2] returned 2.0 for each iron with no warning. Crippen MolLogP(aspirin) = 1.31 against an experimental 1.19. MolWt 180.159 vs ExactMolWt 180.0423. MACCS slice [1:] gives 166.

key_strengths: It actively corrects five widespread myths with the citations that do and do not support them -- the universal AtomPair scaffold-hopping advantage, a universal 4096-bit setting, a fixed collision rate, the '30% of oral drugs violate a rule' figure, and hydrophobe as a Morgan feature invariant. The collision measurement (5.4% to 0.44% across 512-8192 bits) confirms that refusing a fixed number was right.
Nine of the ten tabulated fingerprints construct and behave exactly as tabulated, including the MACCS 167-bit/bit-0 detail and the bit-versus-count divergence for AtomPair and TopologicalTorsion.
The 2D path is fast and clean at library scale: 8,106 mol/s for ECFP4 2048 over 3,224 compounds with only 8 dead bits, and a nine-descriptor panel with zero nan or inf.
The drug-likeness rule sets are transcribed accurately and framed as risk indicators, which is what makes the 371-in-1,000 Ro5 violators in a real hERG set interpretable rather than deletable.
The conformer-dependence warning is quantitatively justified by its own data: atenolol asphericity ranges 0.614-0.824 across a 20-conformer ensemble.

recommendations.title: 3D convergence guard rejects valid ensembles for ordinary flexible drugs
recommendations.problem: Both documented 3D paths raise RuntimeError when any conformer returns MMFF status 1. Status 1 means 'more iterations required', not failure. 19 of 20 conformers for atenolol and 20 of 20 for verapamil hit it, so the snippet discards a usable ensemble for any flexible drug-like molecule. Only the four-carbon example in the Skill succeeds.
recommendations.root_cause: The guard treats MMFFOptimizeMoleculeConfs' two-valued status as pass/fail rather than converged/needs-more-iterations.
recommendations.fix: Pass maxIters=2000 (or higher) and treat status 1 as a warning: count non-converged conformers, re-optimize or drop only those, and raise only when every conformer fails. Update both SKILL.md and examples/calculate_descriptors.py, and add atenolol to the example's __main__ so the path is exercised.

recommendations.title: Version Compatibility pins map4, which has no obtainable distribution
recommendations.problem: The header states the examples were tested with 'map4 1.1+' and the references cite https://pypi.org/project/map4/, but pip reports no version of map4 exists on PyPI and the import fails. MAP4 also appears as a first-class row in the fingerprint taxonomy table.
recommendations.root_cause: The pin was written from the paper and the project README rather than from an actual install.
recommendations.fix: Remove map4 from Version Compatibility, mark the MAP4 taxonomy row as 'GitHub source install, conda-only tmap dependency, no Windows build', and point the stereochemistry-aware route at mapchiral, which does install and works.

recommendations.title: The example's 3D helper is unseeded and non-reproducible
recommendations.problem: calculate_3d_descriptors calls EmbedMolecule(mol, AllChem.ETKDGv3()) with no randomSeed, so three identical calls returned asphericity 0.7876, 0.7216 and 0.7210 -- a 9% swing in a value that may become a QSAR feature. SKILL.md's ensemble snippet does set randomSeed=42.
recommendations.root_cause: Seed management was applied to the SKILL.md pattern and not propagated to the shipped helper.
recommendations.fix: Set params.randomSeed explicitly in calculate_3d_descriptors, accept it as an argument, and state in the usage guide that a recorded seed is required for any descriptor that feeds a model.

recommendations.title: Gasteiger snippet prints charges that do not sum to the formal charge
recommendations.problem: The documented loop iterates the molecule's atoms and prints _GasteigerCharge. For neutral aspirin those sum to -0.6555, because implicit-hydrogen charge is carried separately and the molecule has not had hydrogens added.
recommendations.root_cause: The snippet demonstrates the API call without stating the hydrogen convention it depends on.
recommendations.fix: Call Chem.AddHs before ComputeGasteigerCharges in the snippet, or read _GasteigerHCharge alongside it, and add a line stating that heavy-atom charges alone will not balance.

recommendations.title: No warning that Gasteiger silently echoes formal charge for unparameterised elements
recommendations.problem: ComputeGasteigerCharges on [Fe+2] returned exactly 2.0 with no exception and no nan, so a metal-containing compound passes through a charge-aware pipeline carrying a meaningless number.
recommendations.root_cause: The partial-charge table covers cost and accuracy but not element coverage.
recommendations.fix: Add an element-coverage column or note to the charge table, and show a guard that flags atoms outside the Gasteiger parameter set before the charges are used downstream.

recommendations.title: QED caveat states the wrong failure direction for fragments
recommendations.problem: The Skill warns QED can under-rank fragment-like molecules. Measured the opposite: indole 0.544 and phenol 0.515 clear a 0.5 gate while imatinib, a marketed drug, scores 0.389.
recommendations.root_cause: The caveat generalises the natural-product case, where under-ranking is real (paclitaxel 0.130), to fragments, where the desirability functions are permissive instead.
recommendations.fix: Split the caveat: QED under-ranks large natural-product and peptide chemistry and over-ranks small fragments, with these numbers as worked examples, and repeat that it must not be the sole gate in either regime.
